title: WombatLM
subtitle: A tiny brain learns animal word forms
form.name: copy the name
unknownWord: not an animal from the data
badge.hidden: 🔒 hidden real answer (never seen in training)
badge.invention: ✨ its own invention (no real word in the data)
confidenceHelp: How sure the brain is of the whole word. A sure answer can still be wrong!
score.close: never seen, right or one letter off
att.title: Where it looks
att.help: Each row is one letter of the answer. Dark cells show which letters of the animal the brain looked at while writing it (each row adds up to 100). ✱ is the task (which language and form). Point at a row or at a guess column to link them.
att.decSelf: Looking back at its own answer (head {n})
att.encSelf: Animal letters looking at each other (head {n})
map.title: Letter map
map.help: Every letter is a list of 32 numbers in the brain's letter table. The map squeezes them flat: letters the brain treats alike end up close together. At the start it is a random cloud; watch it sort itself while it learns.
map.note: The flat map shows {a} % + {b} % of the differences between the letters.
inside.intro: This brain has {n} numbers. ChatGPT-class models have hundreds of billions.
inside.help: Every square is one number of the brain. Learning means nudging these numbers a tiny bit after every batch of examples. The weights themselves look like noise; the change shows where it is learning right now.
inside.note.delta: how much each number changed in the last {n} steps
inside.note.grad: which way each number wants to move after the batch of step {step}
inside.note.gradNone: no gradient yet: train at least one step
inside.groupHelp.letters: One row of numbers per letter and per position. The same letter table is used for reading the animal and for choosing the next letter.
inside.groupHelp.encoder: The letters of the animal look at each other and think, so each letter knows its neighbours.
inside.groupHelp.decoder: Letter by letter: look back at the answer so far, look at the animal, think, then guess the next letter.
inside.groupHelp.copy: Decides whether to copy a letter of the animal or write one itself, and which letter to copy.
signal.title: Follow the signal
signal.help: The numbers each position carries on its way through the brain, for {word}. One row per letter, one column per number.
inside.note.delta1: how much each number changed in the last step
build.title: ① Build the brain: learning
build.help: Learning happens only here: while ▶ Play runs, or when you press Step. In every step the brain practises a few examples whose answers it knows, measures its mistakes and nudges all its numbers a little. Nothing else changes the brain.
practice.title: What it's practising now
practice.help: Examples from the latest learning step, each with the right answer. The brain guesses every letter while being shown the correct letters before it, so it can miss one letter and get the next one right. Letters it guessed wrong are red and underlined; ⏎ means it wanted to end the word there. {shown} of the {batch} examples are shown.
practice.empty: Nothing yet. Press ▶ Play or Step ×1 to start learning.
cycle.title: One learning step
cycle.hint: Tip: pause, then press Step ×1 to watch one step slowly.
cycle.running: This repeats about {n} times a second.
ask.title: ② Ask the brain: answering
ask.help: Asking sends your word through the brain once, letter by letter. The brain's numbers are only read, never changed: the same brain always gives the same answer. While it is learning, the answer waits until you pause or press “Ask again” (or tick “keep answering while it learns”).
stamp.fresh: 🔒 Answer from the brain at step {step}. Answering never changes the brain.
stamp.stale: ⏳ The brain has learned {n} more steps since this answer (step {step}).
slow.writing: reading the animal → writing letter {k} of {n}
slow.ending: reading the animal → deciding the word is finished ⏎
